title: fix(console): keep the browser copies of favorites, recents, last app and the pinned list view per organization
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbUq2j5tRRVo3TVY3wcS1Fdg)_
Fixes #36244

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 同时属于两个组织的用户，用同一个浏览器切换组织后，不再在新组织里先看到旧组织的收藏、最近访问、上次应用和固定视图；单组织与无组织部署的用户原有内容保留。
- 为个人设置清点中您接受的建议（p2）：浏览器里的副本跟服务器一样按组织分开保存。
- 出错时最坏是某个组织里的收藏或固定视图首次显示为空、等服务器读回后恢复；不涉及他人数据，撤回本改动即回到原行为。
- 无。

## What changes

- `scopedKey(base, userId, orgId?)` (`UserStateAdapters`) spells `BASE:u:USER:o:ORG` when an organization is active; without one (no organization feature, a preview, the boot before an organization is known) it is the user-only key as before.
- The organization is `ActiveOrganizationStorage`'s id, read synchronously (`useOrganizationScope`): the same id the console stamps on the `sys_user_preference` reads as `X-Tenant-ID`, and the one `switchOrganization` stores before the switch reloads the console, so the first paint after a switch reads the new organization's copy.
- `FavoritesProvider`, `RecentItemsProvider`, `LastAppProvider`, `FlowPaletteRecentsProvider` read and write their browser copy under that key, and re-load when the organization changes. `FavoritesProvider`'s hydrate push-back now reads this organization's local copy, so it can only carry this organization's own nav-pin extras into its row.
- The pinned list view (`list.view.pinned`) is read through `usePinnedListView` (new, `views/pinnedListView.ts`), whose slot is `os:pref:list.view.pinned@object:OBJECT@org:ORG`. Only this preference is keyed this way; the `os:pref` mechanism and every other workspace preference are unchanged.
- **Carry-over rule (Done-when 4):** an organization that finds no copy of its own adopts the copy kept before the organization was part of the key (the user-only `ui.*` copy, and the per-object pin slot): the value moves under that organization's key and the old key is removed, so exactly one organization, the first to read it, inherits it. A single-organization person keeps everything; a deployment with no organization keeps the user-only key unchanged. The first reader is in practice the organization the old copy mirrors: every hydrate rewrote it with the active organization's row, and the first page-load on this code boots into the organization the browser last held.
- Sign-out and change-of-user purges are keep-list sweeps (`purgeSignedOutUserClientState`, `@object-ui/auth`); the new keys are not on the keep list, so they are swept exactly as today's are. A pin in `signOutPurge.test.tsx` holds that for all five new spellings.
- Round 2 (this head): the red `Type Check UI` / `Lint UI` (build) / `Test UI (8/16)` on `f957b6e1` had two causes, both read from the job logs before the fix. (1) `pinnedListView.ts(35,18): error TS2322` — the org slot was built from `objectPreferenceScope()`'s union and could spell `user@org:…`; it is now spelled `object:OBJECT@org:ORG` directly. (2) `FavoritesProvider.test.tsx` "favorites and a nav pin set in A …" read 21 ids — the suite above it leaves its last list under the user-only key, which org A then adopted as designed; the new suite's `beforeEach` now clears storage and resets the mocked user. No production behaviour changed in round 2. `origin/main` was merged once (`b3bcfefc`); it touched only one comment line in `workspacePreference.ts` among this diff's files.

## Tests

Reach measured once, before the fix, by the round-1 dev with a unit harness (no running console with two memberships in this container): real `ActiveOrganizationStorage`, a fake server answering one `ui.favorites` row per stamped organization, favorite + nav pin in A, switch (remount) to B. On base `c30ce97c`: B's first paint `["object:a_obj","nav:a_menu"]` (A's list); B's server row after hydrate `["nav:a_menu"]` (A's nav pin pushed into B); pinned view read in B `"pv_in_org_a"`, back in A after pinning in B `"pv_in_org_b"`, one key `os:pref:list.view.pinned@object:crm_lead`. Both mechanisms reproduce.

All readings below are on head `af1438fd`, under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

Neighbours that read the pin or the preference store (ObjectView.personalViews-29635, ObjectView.titleViewSwitcher-27594, consoleListStateWall-12418, consoleUserPreferenceBudget): `Test Files 4 passed (4)` · `Tests 45 passed (45)` · `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

`ui/packages/app-shell` `pnpm run type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): `VERDICT command-exit 0`, no `error TS`.

<details><summary>Four ablations — each red on its own pins, each restored to the HEAD blob</summary>

- A1 `scopedKey` ignores the organization (`UserStateAdapters.tsx`, blob `94bba20a → 67dd65bb`): `Tests 8 failed | 59 passed` — the per-organization and the adoption pins of all four providers.
- A2 no adoption (`if (own !== null || !userId || !orgId) return own;` → unconditional return; blob `94bba20a → e9c51a34`): `Tests 4 failed | 63 passed` — the four "a single organization keeps the copy …" pins. The first A2 attempt was refused by the tool before anything ran (its replacement text already occurred in the anchor line, so the count did not rise); retried with a distinct replacement.
- A3 pin slot ignores the organization (`pinnedListView.ts`, blob `b49631f8 → af9680b7`): `Tests 2 failed | 65 passed` — the round-trip pin and the single-organization pin.
- A4 no pin adoption (blob `b49631f8 → 6f653efc`): `Tests 1 failed | 66 passed` — the single-organization pin.

After the script: both files' blob equals `HEAD`'s (`94bba20a…`, `b49631f8…`), `git status` clean on both.

## Acceptance notes

- The `os:pref:*` pin slot carries no user. The organization in the slot does not change that, but a different account signing in on the same browser runs the change-of-user purge, which sweeps every key not on its keep list (all `os:pref:*` included), so a second account does not read the first's pin.
- On a browser that holds no active organization yet (first boot, or after the server answered none), the copy is the user-only one until the organization resolves, then the organization adopts it; that boot window also costs one extra preference read when the organization arrives.
- Quiet hours (`notificationPreferences`) still use the user-only key: out of this card.
